subject.title: Feature: Agent 动态切换命令（不重启 Gateway）

question: Should OpenClaw support a user-facing `/agent <id>` temporary conversation switch, and what authorization/state ownership contract must it use?
rationale: The requested feature crosses routing, session ownership, memory isolation, workspace access, and tool credential boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product and security contract safely.

options.title: Add an opt-in secure conversation switch
options.body: Implement a conversation-level configured-agent binding with explicit allowlist/authorization, per-agent session isolation, and bounded cleanup semantics.

options.title: Keep only thread-bound focus commands
options.body: Decline direct-chat `/agent <id>` and steer users to existing `/focus`/thread-bound subagent workflows where supported.

options.title: Defer to channel or plugin-specific experiments
options.body: Keep core unchanged until a plugin proves the user experience and security model without expanding core routing policy.

recommendation.title: Add an opt-in secure conversation switch
recommendation.body: Implement a conversation-level configured-agent binding with explicit allowlist/authorization, per-agent session isolation, and bounded cleanup semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged feature history is PR #21805's thread-bound subagent command and binding stack, which defines the adjacent routing model this feature would need to extend or deliberately avoid.
